name: Epidermal growth factor receptor kinase domain
function_summary: EGFR is a transmembrane receptor tyrosine kinase that transfers phosphate from ATP to protein substrates after ligand-driven activation. Its kinase domain participates in signaling pathways that regulate cell growth and survival.
disease_relevance: Altered EGFR signaling and activating variants are associated with several cancers; small-molecule kinase inhibitors are used in cancer treatment.

key_residues.role: Catalytic lysine in the ATP-binding region; its active-state environment includes a salt bridge with Glu762.
Hinge residue in the ATP pocket; erlotinib’s quinazoline core occupies the hinge region in the 1M17 structure.
The DFG motif marks the start of the activation segment and helps organize catalytic metal and nucleotide interactions.
